hidden_target.material_initial_state: Fine FeCoNiCrAl HEA feedstock powder (5–30 μm), with Al-rich and Cr-rich microsegregated regions and a BCC random-solid-solution structure, deposited onto grit-blasted Inconel 718 substrates (Ra 3.9 ± 0.6 μm).
hidden_target.intervention: Fabrication of an approximately 150 μm FeCoNiCrAl HEA bond coat using the low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 torch with propylene fuel, a 63 mm 3L4 long nozzle, a 2.75 mm powder injector, and the medium air/fuel-pressure setting that gave the best deposition performance; the exact pressures were not provided in the supplied text.
hidden_target.conditions: The substrate was preheated to 155 °C during spraying. Coated specimens underwent isothermal oxidation in air at 1000, 1100, and 1150 °C for up to 50 h, followed by approximately 5 min of air cooling and repeated weighing; exposures beyond 100 h were unsuitable because partial melting of the Inconel 718 substrate compromised coating integrity.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: A highly dense coating with 0.2% porosity, uniform elemental distribution, retained BCC random-solid-solution structure, and only an approximately 3 μm interdiffusion zone; oxidation produced a thin, dense, continuous, predominantly Al2O3 thermally grown oxide layer without substantial mixed chromia/spinel formation.
hidden_target.mechanism: The low-temperature HVAF-i7 process minimizes deposition-stage oxidation and produces low porosity that restricts oxygen ingress and internal oxidation. During exposure, outward diffusion of Al and reaction with oxygen form a protective alumina scale, while the HEA's sluggish elemental diffusion limits oxide transport and mixed-oxide formation, thereby controlling TGO growth. The absence of reactive elements such as Y or Hf may reduce scale adhesion and permit spallation at more severe temperature/time conditions.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to more porous or more oxidized thermal-spray coatings, the dense HVAF-i7 FeCoNiCrAl coating is expected to show enhanced oxidation resistance, less internal oxidation, and slower, controlled growth of a thin continuous alumina TGO; TGO thickness should nevertheless increase with temperature, and spallation may occur under more severe exposure because reactive elements are absent.
hidden_target.baseline: No direct benchmark bond coat was tested. Internal process baselines were low- and high-air/fuel-pressure HVAF-i7 coatings, which had 0.8% and 1.8% porosity and 73% and 53% deposition efficiency, respectively, versus the selected medium-pressure coating; the discussion also qualitatively references coatings with porosity above 6% and literature HVAF-M3/MCrAlY systems.
hidden_target.boundary: The demonstrated intact protective behavior applies to 50 h isothermal exposure at 1000–1150 °C. TGO thickness increased with temperature but not markedly. Claims for longer exposure are limited because Inconel 718 partially melted beyond approximately 100 h; although no visible or cross-sectional Al2O3 spallation was detected after the reported 50 h tests, the paper states that spallation can arise at higher temperature/time because the alloy lacks reactive elements.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: Cross-sectional FESEM with EDS mapping, point analysis, and line scans was used to measure TGO thickness and identify Al/O redistribution and the absence of major mixed oxides; XRD and pseudo-Voigt peak fitting tested phase retention; ImageJ quantified porosity; gravimetric mass gain per total exposed area measured oxidation kinetics, and oxide-collecting crucibles plus visual/cross-sectional inspection tested spallation.
hidden_target.actual_result: At the optimized medium air/fuel setting, deposition efficiency reached 79% and porosity fell to 0.2%, compared with 73%/0.8% and 53%/1.8% at the low and high settings. The approximately 150 μm coating retained its BCC phase and nearly unchanged XRD peak widths, had uniform elemental distribution and an approximately 3 μm interdiffusion zone, and formed a dense, uniform, continuous, predominantly alumina TGO after 50 h at 1000, 1100, and 1150 °C. TGO thickness increased only modestly with temperature and was reported as about 1.8 μm overall; no mixed oxide formation or visible scale spallation was observed after 50 h, indicating controlled oxidation, although susceptibility to later spallation without reactive elements was noted.
